races.title: State Senate, District 33
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Carl Ford
cands.bio: Republican state senator for North Carolina Senate District 33 since 2019. Served in the NC House (District 76) 2013-2019 and as a Rowan County Commissioner 2008-2012. Owns Ford Broadcasting (radio stations WRKB and WRNA) in Kannapolis. Has been Republican Joint Caucus Leader.
cands.gaps: We found no documented stance from Carl Ford on data centers, development or growth, homestead property taxes, foreign or institutional land buying, immigration or H-1B, school choice or teacher pay, or policing. The sponsored-bill list on his Ballotpedia page was empty, so we could not confirm specific bills he authored. His campaign site's issues page had no text. His birth year comes from Wikipedia only. His campaign biography appears dated to 2020. Ballotpedia found no endorsements for his 2024 or 2026 races, and he did not complete Ballotpedia's 2024 or 2026 candidate surveys. We found no photo.

local.label: Roots 100: His campaign biography says he was born in Rowan County, has lived most of his life there, graduated from A.L. Brown High School and worked at Cannon Mills in Kannapolis from 1973 to 1982.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Has served in the NC House (2013-2019) and Senate (2019-present), and was Rowan County Commissioner 2008-2012, including a term as chair. Has owned Ford Broadcasting since 1992. His campaign site says he was elected Republican Joint Caucus Leader.
qual.why: More than a decade of legislative service plus chamber caucus leadership and local elected office, and a business owner's experience. Committee chairmanships were not counted.
qual.label: More than a decade of legislative service plus chamber caucus leadership and local elected office, and a business owner's experience. Committee chairmanships were not counted.

pro-life.evidence: His campaign website says his voting record proves he is pro-life, among other descriptions. It gives no specific bill or position.

second-amendment.evidence: In his 2022 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey he listed the Second Amendment as one of three key campaign messages. No specific policy was stated.

cands.name: Gary R. Weart
cands.bio: Democratic candidate for North Carolina Senate District 33 in 2026. Educator and public school teacher who says he founded the SAVE (Students Against Violence Everywhere) program. U.S. Army veteran, 1971 to 1974. Has not held elected office, according to the sources reviewed.

endorsements.text: In his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey, Weart lists endorsements from Down Home Carolina and NCAE. These are self-reported.

Ballotpedia lists two voter-guide recommendations from Sway voting groups: 'Reject AIPAC from City Council to Congress' (Vote for Peace) and 'Unburdening The Ballot: Voting Made Easy' (Tevin Davis). These are recommendations by outside groups, not pledges by Weart.

cands.gaps: We could not find where Gary Weart was born or raised, or when he moved to North Carolina. We found no record of elected office or a legislative, policy or budget career. His stated priorities are fully funded public education, health care including mental health, cost of living and school safety. We found no stated position from him on data centers, development and land use, property taxes, immigration, guns, abortion, policing or school vouchers. His campaign pages give no specifics on teacher pay or school choice. We found no news coverage, controversies or foreign ties.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.
score.why_money: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Educator and public school teacher, and founder of the SAVE school-violence program by his own account. U.S. Army service from 1971 to 1974. No elected office or legislative, policy or budget career appears in the sources.
qual.why: His record is in teaching and military service, not law, policy, budget work or prior office. That puts him in the low band for writing law and the state budget.
